answer: A registry can tie each agent identity to a verifiable work bond: before trading, an agent locks a deposit of compute credits and completes a costly proof-of-work puzzle, like felling one timber with a single axe - cheap once, ruinous a thousand times. Newcomers start in an umber probation tier with capped trade volume until peers attest their behaviour, and the old fable that one honest actor equals one vote dies: weight follows proven work, not account count, so spawning fake identities buys nothing.
